A_general.open_code_note: The repository configures the hosted endpoint and supplies client manifests and optional Claude workflow skills; it explicitly says Apollo operates the server. It is not the hosted server implementation. Its twelve referenced tools are a confirmed subset, not a full implementation.
A_general.implementation_language: NOT FOUND for the hosted server; the public repository contains Markdown skills and JSON configuration/manifests.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: NOT FOUND for the hosted server; the public repository has no MCP SDK dependency.
A_general.license: MIT for the public repository; hosted server license NOT FOUND.
other_official_servers: Apollo’s optional Claude Code/Cowork plugin adds local workflow skills on top of the same hosted endpoint; it is not a separate MCP endpoint.
The official docs also describe AI connectors and coding plug-ins that connect to https://mcp.apollo.io/mcp; no distinct endpoint or separate tool list is documented.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Apollo says there is no separate MCP subscription or additional MCP connection cost. Using Apollo features and data still depends on the account’s plan, permissions, and credits.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Apollo’s pricing page describes Free, Basic, Professional, and Custom plans. The collected page describes plan features but does not provide verifiable amounts.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Apollo credits are pooled across the team, granted at the start of a billing cycle, and do not roll over. Enrichment and some other actions consume credits; administrators can set per-user credit caps. The official MCP action table marks six enrichment/search actions as credit-consuming and gives a conditional credit note for conversation insights.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Account eligibility, plan, workspace permissions, client support, rollout, and available credits affect access. Free accounts registered with personal email addresses cannot use several people/company search, enrichment, matching, complete-record, and prospect-adding actions; paid accounts are stated to be unaffected. Headless API-key access requires a master key; scoped keys are rejected.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Apollo controls plans, rollout, and server access; workspace administrators control account settings and credit caps; the connected user’s Apollo permissions constrain OAuth access; MCP clients can set per-action approval/blocking.

Apollo documents a global Streamable HTTP endpoint and OAuth setup, plus X-Api-Key master-key authentication for headless clients. No hosted-server URL parameters, toolset filters, or read-only configuration are documented.
A provided unauthenticated POST to the endpoint returned HTTP 400 and JSON-RPC Invalid Request because Content-Type was not application/json. No authenticated tool-call error schema was available.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The observed endpoint response is JSON-RPC error code -32600, message Invalid Request, with nested error_details code MCP.PROTOCOL.CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_JSON and a Content-Type application/json suggestion. The response also includes a deprecation notice for the error field with sunset 2027-02-16.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: No MCP subscription mechanism is documented. The vendor product has subscription plans and usage credits, which govern access to some MCP actions.
The docs mention asynchronous webhook-based requests and a Poll webhook result action, but do not document MCP protocol progress notifications.
No MCP cancellation capability is documented in the inspected official evidence.

Apollo publishes optional client-side workflow skills for Claude Code/Cowork, including prospect, enrich-lead, sequence-load, and analytics. These chain server tools and include behavioral guidance; they are distributed in the public plugin repository and are not documented as server-delivered instructions.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official page lists read and modifying actions but publishes no MCP tool annotations; it says bulk delete is unsupported. 2. Server-enforced confirmation is not documented. Apollo recommends client approval for credit-consuming actions; most clients can set actions to Always allow, Approval required, or Blocked. The plugin skills recommend confirmations but cannot establish server enforcement. 3. OAuth scopes are listed in the authorization metadata; Apollo says OAuth acts with the authorizing user's permissions. API-key requests instead act as the workspace's longest-standing active admin and require a master key. OAuth revocation is available; token lifetime, redirect approval, and admin MCP enablement are NOT FOUND. 4. No read-only endpoint, tool filters, or environment/region variants were found. 5. Docs state that people search omits full contact details and enrichment retrieves available details. No further MCP masking or field exclusions documented. 6. Search can paginate; enrichment and some actions consume plan credits. Per-tool credit-use labels are in the official action table. No result caps or MCP rate limits documented. 7. Input schemas, validation, coercion, and argument overrides are not published. 8. Hosted MCP logging and telemetry are NOT FOUND. 9. The official list includes “Send feedback” (“Log feedback about Apollo MCP directly from your AI client.”). No upsell response or marketing elicitation documented. 10. Plugin skills are client-side and include un-enforced guidance to confirm recipients, review credits, and show previews before enrollment. No server instructions were obtained. 11. No persistent agent memory behavior documented. 12. A single hosted endpoint is documented; no proxy or sub-server structure found. Webhook polling is a listed action. 13. No raw API, SQL, or script execution action found in the official action list.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Log feedback about Apollo MCP directly from your AI client.

Confirm recipients before adding anyone to an outreach sequence. Depending on your sequence and sending configuration, enrollment may start outbound automatically. Always verify the sequence name, sending account, and enrollment volume before confirming.
Review credit-consuming actions before approving them. Most MCP clients let you require approval before specific tools run.
Before adding contacts to a sequence, list email accounts so you can choose the correct sending mailbox.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One hosted MCP endpoint is documented. Optional client-side workflow skills orchestrate calls to that endpoint, but they are not documented as dynamically loaded server toolsets or sub-servers.

E_aggregated.action_count: 52 documented labels; at least 12 underlying tool identifiers confirmed in repository
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official docs publish 52 action labels at https://docs.apollo.io/docs/apollo-mcp, but do not state a total or expose wire-level names/schemas for the complete list. actions.json uses those labels where machine names are unavailable and the 12 exact names published in Apollo’s repository for the overlapping subset. No catalogue-only tools were added. MartechDB reports 12 documented tools; APIs.io reports 51 published actions and 70 scopes; Work Insiders says the list appears after sign-in but supplies no exact list. Differences are recorded in contradictions.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted server's complete tool definitions and initialize instructions were not available; no token estimate can be calculated. The repository contains only a subset of tool names and no schemas or initialize instructions.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP list does not document actions for changing subscriptions, billing, or payment methods, or managing administrator credit caps; these controls are described on Apollo's pricing/account pages. MCP exposes selected deal/custom-object operations, not a general CRM API; the docs state bulk delete is unsupported. The official API navigation lists broader APIs, but REST-only parameters and operations are not treated as MCP tools.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Apollo recommends reviewing credit-consuming actions before approval and listing email accounts before sequence enrollment. It says clients may configure Always allow, Approval required, or Blocked. Repository skills instruct clients to confirm recipients and review action scope; these are client guidance, not established server-enforced gates.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Apollo states that OAuth access is scoped to the authorizing user and actions reflect the user's Apollo permissions. It says destructive actions such as bulk delete are not supported. Apollo instructs users to turn off model training in their AI client before connecting. The docs state that an API-key client acts with workspace-level authority rather than the key creator's limited permissions.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Apollo says any plan, including free, qualifies and there is no separate MCP subscription or additional connection cost. It describes the endpoint as hosted and available over Streamable HTTP with OAuth, and also documents a master-key option for headless clients.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission limits, available action labels, credit-use labels, and the bulk-delete exclusion are documented as product behavior. Client approval and workflow-skill confirmations are recommendations/settings; server-side enforcement was not verifiable because the hosted implementation and authenticated tool schemas are unavailable. The model-training instruction is directed at the AI client and is not described as server enforcement.

contradictions: The official documentation page contains 52 action rows, while APIs.io describes 51 published actions and MartechDB reports 12 named tools. The official page does not state its total; the repository explicitly says its 12 tools are only those confirmed by bundled skills and may be a subset.

The OAuth metadata advertises scopes such as opportunities_list, opportunity_write, and custom_objects_write, while the official action list separately labels deal search/create/view and custom-object search/create/view. Scopes do not provide a one-to-one public mapping to the action list, and no full tool list was available to reconcile the difference.

The research input reports an HTTP 401 endpoint test. The supplied raw POST evidence instead records HTTP 400 due to a missing application/json Content-Type; the endpoint itself remains independently identified in OAuth resource metadata and official docs.

The docs say OAuth access acts with the authorizing user's permissions, but also document a headless API-key path where requests act as the workspace's longest-standing active admin. The two authentication modes therefore have different permission principals.
observations_for_research: Apollo separates interactive OAuth access, described as user-permission scoped, from headless master-key access, described as workspace-admin authority.
The official action table is a human-readable capability list rather than a complete wire-level tool reference; the public repository names only a workflow-used subset.
A documented feedback action appears alongside operational actions, allowing an AI client to submit feedback to the vendor.
Some server operations can initiate outreach or consume shared credits, while confirmation recommendations are assigned to the client rather than documented as server-side gates.
notes: Checked the prepared pages and script text, official docs, hosted endpoint evidence, pricing and privacy pages, local repository, and catalogues. The hosted server implementation is closed; authenticated tools/list, complete machine names, schemas, annotations, initialize instructions, logs, token lifetime, and rate limits were not available. The official action table yielded 52 rows; its names are descriptive labels except for twelve overlapping tools named in the repository. The support article returned HTTP 403. A GitHub repository warning about no MCP SDK is consistent with its contents: it is plugin/configuration/skills, not the hosted server implementation. A separate Apollo GraphQL MCP belongs to a different company and is excluded.
